name: Asymptotic Growth Notation
description: Asymptotic analysis provides a mathematical foundation for describing the limiting behavior of functions. It utilizes Big-O, Omega, and Theta notations to classify algorithms by their resource consumption.
common_pitfalls: Confusing worst-case performance with upper bounds
Ignoring constant factors when they matter practically

name: Formal Proofs of Correctness
description: Establishing algorithmic correctness requires rigorous mathematical induction over structural or computational steps. This ensures that the algorithm terminates and yields the expected output for all valid inputs.
common_pitfalls: Neglecting the base case in inductive proofs

name: Loop Invariants
description: Loop invariants are properties that hold true before and after each iteration of a loop. They serve as the primary mechanism for proving the correctness of iterative algorithms.
common_pitfalls: Weakening the invariant so it does not imply postconditions

name: Recursive Problem Solving
description: Recursion involves breaking a problem down into smaller instances of the same problem until reaching a base case. It forms the algorithmic foundation for divide-and-conquer strategies.
common_pitfalls: Infinite recursion due to missing or flawed base cases
High memory overhead from unoptimized call stacks

name: Recursion Trees
description: Recursion trees visually map out the cost of recursive function calls at each level of execution. They are instrumental in intuitively solving recurrences before applying formal methods.
common_pitfalls: Miscalculating the number of leaves or tree height
Errors in summing the work done across levels

name: The Master Theorem
description: The Master Theorem provides a cookbook method for resolving recurrence relations of the form commonly arising in divide-and-conquer algorithms. It categorizes asymptotic bounds based on parameters comparing work at different levels.
common_pitfalls: Applying the theorem when the recurrence does not fit the standard form

name: Advanced Recurrence Relations
description: Advanced recurrence analysis addresses complex dependencies where standard cookbook methods fail. Techniques such as substitution and generating functions are employed to derive tight bounds.
common_pitfalls: Guessing an incorrect inductive hypothesis in the substitution method
